## Design note

The top of the market. A shrieking 8500 rpm V10, instant dual-clutch shifts and all-wheel drive make it the quickest car off the line in any weather, and it keeps pulling past where the old exotic runs out of breath. The AWD front split tames the mid-engine snap a little, but it is still light at the front and rotates hard on a lift. Wins pay like nothing else; a crash costs a small house.

## How this car breaks

Aluminium spaceframe with carbon-fibre panels: much stiffer and safer than the 90s exotic's, but everything behind the bulkhead is still sacrificial — the rear subframe carries the V10, gearbox and rear suspension, so rear hits kill drive. The front diff and radiators sit in a short nose with little crumple length. Panels crack and tear rather than dent. Durability class 3: the bonded aluminium/CFRP cell takes a 56 km/h frontal like a modern car, which the 90s exotic cannot.

## Inertia

Box approximation about the CG, scaled for mass concentration (`k < 1`: mass near the centre, e.g. mid-engine; `k → 1`: mass at the ends):

```
I_roll  = k_r · m·(W² + H²)/12
I_pitch = k_p · m·(L² + H²)/12
I_yaw   = k_y · m·(W² + L²)/12
```

| pitch | 2895 | 0.75 | 2170 |

## Engine

5.2 L DOHC 40-valve V10, naturally aspirated, dual injection, dry sump. Class-typical 2010s NA 5.2 V10 (~86 kW/L, ~449 kW at 8250 rpm, ~560 N·m at 6500) per manufacturer spec-class data and owner dyno sheets; torque builds steadily to a high peak, as NA V10s do.

Peak **449 kW @ 8250 rpm**, **560 N·m @ 6500 rpm**. Idle 1000 / redline 8500 / limiter 8700 rpm. Rotating inertia 0.15 kg·m² (class: 0.10 small four … 0.30 big-block). Engine braking 10% of peak torque = 56 N·m. Power-to-weight 275 kW/t.

## Drivetrain

7-speed dual-clutch, permanent AWD (fixed 30 % front split, centre coupling modelled as a fixed split), open front diff, clutch-type rear LSD. Layout **AWD, 30 % front**; front diff: open; rear diff: clutch LSD, preload 60 N·m, power ramp 0.45, coast ramp 0.30. Clutch capacity 1.40 × peak torque = 780 N·m. Shift time 0.15 s.

## Suspension

Springs from ride frequency, `k = m_s·(2πf)²` with sprung corner mass `m_s = axle load/2 − unsprung`; dampers `c = 2ζ·√(k·m_s)`, ζ = 0.32 bump, rebound = 1.5 × bump.

| Axle | m_s | f | Wheel rate k | Bump c | Rebound c | Travel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Front | 321 kg | 2.05 Hz | 53300 N/m | 2650 N·s/m | 3980 N·s/m | 0.11 m |
| Rear | 448 kg | 2.25 Hz | 89500 N/m | 4050 N·s/m | 6080 N·s/m | 0.12 m |

Round 12b ride rule (A): the file carries the derived dampers × 1.2 bump / × 1.6 rebound (rebound ≈ 2 × bump), after any tunes below: **3180 / 6370 N·s/m F, 4860 / 9730 N·s/m R** (bump / rebound).

Anti-roll bars from a roll-gradient target of 1.5°/g with 52% of roll stiffness at the front. Roll arm h − h_rc = 0.317 m (roll centres 0.08 m F / 0.12 m R). Required total K_φ = m·g·arm/φ = 193981 N·m/rad; springs give k·t²/2 = 74300 F / 120378 R N·m/rad; bars supply the rest as `arb_n_per_m = K_bar/t²` = **9500 F / 0 R N/m** (clamped at ≥ 0). Resulting gradient 1.3°/g, front share 46%. Bump stops 200000 N/m.

Alignment: camber -1.2° F / -1.6° R, toe +0.00° F / +0.20° R (+ = in), caster 7.0°.

## Brakes

Full-pedal line pressure 100 bar.

- Front: 380 mm disc, pistons per side 38 mm + 36 mm + 32 mm → A = 29.6 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 165 mm, pad μ = 0.45: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.45·100 bar·29.6 cm²·0.165 m = **4390 N·m**
- Rear: 356 mm disc, pistons per side 38 mm + 34 mm → A = 20.4 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 153 mm, pad μ = 0.43: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.43·100 bar·20.4 cm²·0.153 m = **2687 N·m**

ABS ceiling: caliper capacity 4390 / 2687 N·m exceeds 1.5 × the front lock torque on this car's tire (peak μ 1.20), which `wp_vehicle`'s ABS cannot modulate (it releases to a fraction of the commanded torque, so an oversized caliper keeps the wheel locked). Both axles scaled by 0.63 → **2750 / 1680 N·m**. Remove when 02's ABS modulates relative to lock torque.

Lock check at 1 g on μ = 1 (load transfer m·a·h/L): front needs 1528 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.80×), rear needs 1174 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.43×).

`wp_vehicle` gives the axle `bias_front` favours its full `max_torque_*` and scales the other by (1 − b)/b, so `max_torque_*` holds the caliper capacity per wheel and `bias_front` acts as the proportioning valve: the rear is trimmed to the same lock margin as the front (ideal rear = T_f · lock_r/lock_f = 2113 N·m), never boosted above its caliper capacity. Rear capacity is below that (hardware-limited rear), so `bias_front` = **0.5**: both axles get full caliper torque → delivered 2750 N·m front / 1680 N·m rear per wheel at full pedal. Handbrake 2420 N·m per rear wheel.

## Steering

Ratio 15.0:1. Kerb-to-kerb turning circle 11.5 m → outer-front path radius 5.63 m, rear-axle-centre radius 4.13 m → mean road-wheel lock δ = atan(L/R) = **0.571 rad (32.7°)** (outer 28.1°, inner 38.8° at full Ackermann; `ackermann_frac` 0.50). Rack speed 1.7 rad/s.

## Damage lattice (`data/lattices/fulmine_v10.json`)

276 nodes, 1772 beams, 6 detachables, 21 component mounts.

- Generated with `gen-lattice --id fulmine_v10 --profile coupe --width 1.95 --length 4.46 --height 1.17 --wheelbase 2.65 --mass 326.8 --car-mass 1634.1 --clearance 0.11 --front-overhang 0.93 --strength 1.0` (20% of vehicle mass in the lattice; strength from durability class 3).
- Era `2010s`: gen-lattice's default HSS passenger cell kept as is.
- Aluminium body: 610 outer-panel beams mild_steel → aluminum.
- Mid-engine: engine block moved behind the cabin bulkhead (y -0.87…-1.52 m), mounted to the rear rails and the bulkhead; 10 nodes behind the bulkhead relabelled FrameRear (engine bay, not cabin); 16 front-rail beams × 1.6 (no engine block in the nose: they get gen-lattice's rear-rail factor); 166 rear-subframe beams → aluminum ×1.5 section (sacrificial); gearbox and half-shafts at the rear axle, side fuel tanks at the sills behind the seats; engine fails at 0.12 m, gearbox 0.08 m.
